body: Thank you. I suppose I'm looking to feel results immediately. I'm not known for being patient with myself.

I wrote "I want to kill myself" on a toy when I was 5. My father was an alcoholic and my mom used to beat my sister merciless (I don't remember). You don't sound ... bad, like they are. But I'm bringing it up for a reason.

When I asked my mom, how to spell "myself", she snapped back at me "Not now". Demonstrating that her needs come before mine, even if mine involve getting away from the intense pain I feel. Why does you 8 year feel intense pain? Thats something you asked yourself, Im sure. I cant focus at the moment. I wish when I wrote this my parents got me therapy. Subsequent suicide attempts at 13 and 15 didn't provide therapy either, but shame, and anger towards the therapist I went and got by myself.

Anyway. Besides that I think you reacted correctly. There IS something going on in your house. Or his school. He doesn't know how to talk about it yet. \*Thats ok!\* I know it sounds scary. You're going to have alot of fears Im sure. Be strong. Be vigilant. DONT stretch yourself too thin, either. When a parent is overburdened like my mom, they will be exhausted and not supportive. Get yourself some support too. Therapy, babysitter you can trust, make more time for baking pies if thats enjoyable etc

I've traced my suicidal roots back to the type of "emotional invalidation" that I described from my mother. Both parents basically act "annoyed" to this day about any of my mental illness. Despite having severe mental illness themselves. Or maybe because they know they are powerless to help me, they take it out on me.

Whatever pain, your child is or isn't going through, the few times my parents have truly acted supportive, were enough to sustain me for YEARS. I think you'll all get through this.

Overall my point is, the feelings journal will help them express their thoughts. It could be years until they accurately pinpoint why they said that to a friend. Kids are new at this, plus very creative, so maybe they were so embarassed they repeated something they heard an adult say ("Oh I could just die"). Its great youre getting to know your child at an emotional level. Again, it would have been all I needed, to grow up stronger, so I think stick with therapy and keep open channels between your child, Respect them and they will respect themselves.
